item.title: Soludo presents APGA flag to Tinubu as 2027 flagbearer
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has formally presented the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) flag to President Bola Tinubu, declaring the party’s support for his re-election bid in the 2027 general election. The symbolic presentation took place at Alex Ekwueme Square, Awka, during the “SoluTinubu 2027” mega rally, where Vice President Kashim Shettima received the flag on behalf of Tinubu. Addressing party members and political leaders at the rally, Soludo said the gesture represented an effort to integrate the South-East into mainstream national politics. “We are representing APGA, and we are presenting our own party flag to the President,” the governor said. He urged Anambra residents to reconsider their voting pattern in the 2027 presidential election, recalling that Tinubu secured only 0.8 per cent of the votes cast in the state in the 2023 presidential election, compared with the 73 per cent mandate Soludo secured during his second-term governorship election. Soludo said the rally followed weeks of statewide town hall engagements organised by his party, which he described as conversations centred on the collective survival and prosperity of the Igbo people. Acknowledging existing grievances and political sentiments in the South-East, he argued that the region could not afford to remain politically isolated. “In a democracy, what leverage do we have other than our votes and alliance with the whole country? What do we gain by wasting our votes again?” he asked. He argued that supporting a Southern president to complete an eight-year tenure before power rotates to the North would provide the South-East with greater political leverage and opportunities to secure federal infrastructure projects and address regional security concerns. The governor also expressed confidence in the Tinubu-Shettima ticket, claiming that the administration’s economic and development agenda had not been matched by a credible opposition alternative. He urged the people of the South-East to support the President’s re-election bid, describing the political alignment as an opportunity for the region to strengthen its participation in national affairs. Receiving the flag on Tinubu’s behalf, Shettima commended the people of Anambra for their turnout and assured the state and the wider South-East of the Federal Government’s commitment to fulfilling its campaign promises if re-elected. The rally also attracted several political leaders, including Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma; Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu; Minister of Works, Dave Umahi; former Anambra State Governor, Chris Ngige; and Senator Adams Oshiomhole. The leaders urged grassroots mobilisers to canvass support for Tinubu across party lines and at polling units, stressing the need for greater political integration of the South-East into national politics. item.title: State health budgets rise 67% to ₦3.3tn — Pate
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Combined health budgets of state governments across Nigeria have increased by more than 67 per cent, from ₦1.97 trillion in 2023 to over ₦3.3 trillion in 2026, while national health insurance enrolment has risen by 50 per cent, from 16 million to nearly 24 million people within the same period. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the opening of the 67th National Council on Health (NCH) in Lafia, Nasarawa State, with the theme, “From Commitments to Results.” Pate said Nigeria had fulfilled 41 presidential health sector commitments and recorded improvements in 12 of 13 core national health indicators since the launch of the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative in December 2023. Highlighting progress in healthcare delivery and financial protection, the minister said skilled birth deliveries in health facilities supported by the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) increased from 4.8 million in 2023 to nearly eight million by mid-2026. He added that fourth antenatal care visits also rose from six million to 8.7 million within the period. According to him, emergency transport systems have conveyed more than 100,000 women and newborns to healthcare facilities, while the Federal Government’s free emergency obstetric care initiative has funded more than 80,000 caesarean sections. He said over 50,000 patients had also accessed free 48-hour emergency care across 507 empanelled facilities, while more than 5,000 patients benefited from dialysis subsidies of up to 80 per cent. On healthcare workforce development, Pate said the proportion of health facilities with at least two midwives or community health workers had increased from 12 per cent to nearly 91 per cent nationally. He said nearly 20,000 skilled birth attendants had been recruited across 22 states, alongside almost 5,000 community health workers in 10 states, while close to 80,000 frontline health workers had undergone retraining. On immunisation, the minister said vaccination campaigns had reached more than 100 million children aged zero to nine with measles and rubella vaccines, while over 70 million adolescent girls had received the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine against cervical cancer. He further disclosed that 10 domestic health manufacturing factories and production lines were now producing medicines, rapid diagnostic test kits, mosquito nets and medical oxygen, with six commissioned in 2026 alone. He said the development was supported by more than ₦24 billion in tax waivers granted under President Bola Tinubu’s June 2024 Executive Order. Despite the progress, Pate warned that Nigerian households continued to bear a disproportionate share of healthcare costs through out-of-pocket payments. item.title: Missing medical records force Nigerians to repeat tests, spend more on healthcare – Survey
item.description: … Two in five patients pay twice for same laboratory tests, scans … 61.5% seek better hospital processes, information management By Chioma Obinna Poor medical records management and failure of health facilities to make patients’ previous test results and medical histories readily accessible are forcing Nigerians to repeat laboratory investigations and scans, worsening the financial burden of accessing healthcare, a new survey has revealed. The Nigerian Health Continuity Survey, involving 1,820 adults across the six geopolitical zones and the Federal Capital Territory, found that two in five respondents had paid at least once in the past two years to repeat a laboratory test or scan because the previous result could not be found. The proportion increased to 52.1 per cent among respondents who gave definite answers to the question, excluding those who were unsure. Almost half of those affected said they had paid for repeated tests more than once. The findings expose another dimension of Nigeria’s healthcare affordability crisis, showing how administrative inefficiencies, poor information management and weak continuity of care are adding avoidable expenses to the already high cost of medical treatment. Conducted online between November 5 and 12, 2026, the survey examined patients’ experiences in retrieving previous medical records, accessing healthcare and managing the financial and time costs of hospital visits. It found that 47.3 per cent of 1,480 respondents who had attempted to retrieve information from previous hospital visits, tests or prescriptions described the process as somewhat or very difficult. Only 18.9 per cent said it was very easy. The time required to access healthcare was another major concern. Of respondents who reported the duration of their most recent care journey, 73.4 per cent said they spent at least two hours from leaving home to completing their hospital visit, while 17.6 per cent said the process took a full day or longer. The financial implications were equally significant, with 41.8 per cent spending more than N50,000 on their most recent healthcare journey, including transportation and medicines. Another 25.3 per cent spent more than N100,000. The survey also found that 65.9 per cent of healthcare journeys were organised by patients or their families, while health facilities organised only 13.2 per cent. This means that responsibilities such as booking appointments, arranging transportation, making phone calls, handling payments and following up on treatment largely rested on households. Significantly, the survey found that patients’ concerns extended beyond the affordability of healthcare. item.title: Sambo hails Buhari’s legacy of integrity, discipline
item.description: By Femi Bolaji Former Minister of Transportation, Mu’azu Jaji Sambo, has described the late former President Muhammadu Buhari as a leader whose commitment to truth, integrity and discipline shaped his approach to national development. Sambo stated this in a message to newsmen while commenting on the public presentation of Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography, authored by Udo Yakubu. He described the publication as a laudable initiative that documents Buhari’s life, leadership and contributions to national development. According to him, “President Buhari took a path of truth, integrity and discipline to build a great Nigeria. “The three-volume biography is an important historical intervention that will enable present and future generations to appreciate the late President’s place in Nigeria’s history.” Sambo said the Buhari administration represented an important chapter in Nigeria’s democratic and developmental journey, adding that its policies, institutional foundations and national direction remained relevant to the country’s continuing development. He noted that the three-volume biography, comprising Buhari the Phenomenon, Buhari the Presidency and Buhari the Reckoning, chronicles the late President’s life, political journey, administration and historical significance. The ceremony was chaired by former President of Niger Republic, Mahamadou Issoufou, while the steering committee was led by former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Boss Mustapha. The formal unveiling was performed by former President Goodluck Jonathan, who was represented at the event by former Senate President, Senator Pius Anyim. item.title: [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally
item.description: There was a mild drama at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Anambra State on Thursday when a former governor of the state, Chris Ngige, urged residents to vote for the APC in the 2027 presidential, National Assembly, and House of Assembly elections. The former Minister of Labour and Employment, who spoke in Igbo, said Anambra residents had one target. “We will vote for the APC from top to bottom,” Ngige said, prompting reactions from participants at the rally, including Governor Charles Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), who stood beside him on stage and told his predecessor that the rally is a joint one. The former governor, who said he was not surprised by the reactions, later told members of APGA to vote for candidates of their choice. “Okay, members of APGA — freedom of choice — when you get to the polling booth, vote for the better place,” he said. Ngige added that while people were free to choose between APGA and the APC, Anambra desires to be connected to the Federal Government at the centre and get it through the ruling party. Earlier, the former minister said he remains a member of the APC, claiming that he brought the party to the South-East. “I am still a member of the APC, bona fide member, because I brought APC to the South East — 2013/2014,” he said. “The only thing is that I told people I am on sabbatical, but even if I am on sabbatical, my governor cannot be doing something, and the Vice President is coming physically, and the governor has called me to say we are here, and I would say I won’t come. No.” Ngige said people should not be forced but persuaded to vote during the 2027 general election. He also said those stopping people from campaigning are not doing so in the name of the APC. “We don’t want that — destruction of vehicles, stoning of people. No! We don’t want that. We must emulate other people practising democracy,” the former Anambra governor said. “Democracy gives you the right of choice; even inside the same family, you must exercise that.” Watch Ngige’s remarks in the video below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] Drama As Ngige Urges Residents To Vote For APC ‘From Top To Bottom’ At Anambra Presidential Rally appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tinubu not anti-Igbo, his son married an Igbo woman – Shettima
item.description: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has dismissed allegations that President Bola Tinubu is hostile towards the Igbo, citing his son Seyi’s marriage to a woman with Igbo heritage as evidence of his affinity with the ethnic group. Shettima made the remark on Thursday at the All Progressives Congress’ SoluTinubu 2027 campaign rally in Awka, Anambra State, where he appealed to the South-East to support Tinubu’s re-election bid. “President Tinubu is a friend of Ndigbo. His son, Seyi, is married to a lady of Igbo extraction. If he hates the Igbo, he couldn’t have allowed his son to marry an Igbo lady,” he said. The vice-president added that the Igbo remained an important part of Nigeria, saying, “So we are essentially one people. The Igbos are an essential component of the Nigerian configuration.” Seyi Tinubu is married to Layal Jade Tinubu, a Nigerian-Lebanese entrepreneur and philanthropist whose maternal heritage is linked to Anambra State. The couple married in August 2016, with celebrations held in Lagos and at Villa Erba, Lake Como, Italy. Their Italian wedding ceremony took place on August 10, 2016. item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council’s media directorate, Obafemi George, has questioned former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s claim that the North-West and North-East would vote for him, arguing that President Bola Tinubu has stronger support. George said this during an interview on Arise News’ Morning Show on Thursday, citing Atiku’s son’s move to the APC and support for Tinubu as he challenged Atiku’s claim to votes in the two regions. “Vice President Atiku Abubakar is boasting that Northwest and Northeast would vote for him. When his own biological son left his party, moved to APC, and he’s campaigning for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. So if Atiku Abubakar cannot even convince his own biological son of his capacity to lead Nigeria, you now think that 25 million voters in Northwest will believe him?” George said. He also questioned whether the African Democratic Congress (ADC) could convince Nigerians that it had a plan, citing the political choice of the party’s national chairman Senator David Mark’s daughter. “The chairman of ADC, Senator David Mark, his own biological daughter in Benue, is contesting in Otukwu Oyimini federal constituency as House of Representatives member. Guess what? From which political party? APC. So if the chairman of a party cannot convince his own daughter to stay with his party, why should Nigerians believe that they have a plan?” he said. George said politicians could assess their own chances of winning, as he defended Tinubu’s record and described him as the only candidate with the capacity and track record to lay a foundation that could sustain Nigeria for decades. “A politician knows whether he’s going to lose an election or he’s going to win an election,” he said. “In this 2027 election, there is only one candidate that has the track record, that has the capacity, that has the audacity to lay the kind of foundation that will sustain Nigeria for the next 40, 50 years, and that candidate is President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” George said. George, who has worked in real estate for 25 years, compared Tinubu’s leadership to laying a building’s foundation. He said the president had laid foundations in security, education, the economy, infrastructure and health, adding: “None of those candidates stand anywhere near him.” The APC campaign council member also argued that the pressures Nigerians face from high living costs are not unique to the country, citing Germany, France, Italy and Portugal. item.title: INEC assures Nigerians of neutrality in 2027 elections
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has assured Nigerians of its neutrality and commitment to conducting credible 2027 general elections. The INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance on Thursday in Abuja, at the 2026 Annual Lecture and Awards of the Association of Corporate Online Editors (ACOE). The INEC chairman spoke on the theme: “Roadmap to 2027: Strengthening Electoral Security Through Collaboration between INEC, the Media, and Political Parties for Credible and Hitch-Free Elections”. Amupitan, represented by his Chief Press Secretary, Mr Adebayo Oketola, said the commission would not serve as an appendage of any political party, whether in government or opposition. He also said that the commission remained committed to institutional neutrality, legal compliance and transparent administration of the electoral process. According to him, INEC has conducted four major off-cycle elections and 16 legislative by-elections since the current leadership assumed office in October 2025. He said the exercises provided opportunities to identify operational weaknesses, assess logistics and strengthen procedures ahead of the 2027 general elections. The INEC boss reiterated that the presidential and National Assembly elections would hold on Jan. 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections would take place on Feb. 6, 2027. He disclosed that INEC would conduct a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Nov. 28, 2026, across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. He revealed that the commission had strengthened its result-uploading and validation procedures to address concerns surrounding result transmission. He also explained that polling unit figures entered on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV). He added that more than 1.6 million invalid, duplicate and deceased entries had been removed from the voter register. Amupitan further disclosed that the commission had procured 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices. “INEC has reduced the number of voters assigned to each BVAS device from 1,250 to 850 to minimise accreditation delays. “The commission has also made provisions for 232,658 persons with disabilities registered to vote,” he said. On electoral security, the INEC chairman said, that the commission was working with the Office of the National Security Adviser and the Nigeria Police Force through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security. He said the collaboration would be extended to state, local government and registration area levels to protect electoral personnel, materials and voters. Amupitan identified misinformation, disinformation, synthetic voice cloning, manipulated videos and coordinated information manipulation as major threats to the 2027 elections. item.title: Buhari told me he would always do what was right, regardless of who was involved — BUA chairman
item.description: By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor The Chairman of BUA Group, Alhaji Abdul Samad Rabiu, has recounted how former President Muhammadu Buhari stood by him during a difficult period in his business, insisting that he would always do what was right, irrespective of those involved. Rabiu said Buhari’s commitment to justice and fairness helped save his business when he faced challenges with some government agencies. He disclosed this in a goodwill message delivered on his behalf by Senator Lawal Shuaibu at the launch of Buhari: The Authorised Biography. The message was shared by Buhari’s former Senior Special Assistant on Media and Publicity, Garba Shehu, on his X handle on Thursday. Describing Buhari as a father, mentor, trusted friend and pillar of strength to him and his family, Rabiu said the former President stood by him during some of the most difficult moments of his life and business. He recalled facing enormous challenges with certain government agencies, which he said threatened the survival of his business and years of investment. According to him, Buhari stood firmly on the side of justice despite strong resistance and pressure from those who wanted him to act otherwise. “I remember vividly when he assured me that he would always do what was right, regardless of who was involved or how powerful they might be. I was moved to tears by those words and by his genuine concern for me,” he said. Rabiu said Buhari’s determination to uphold justice ultimately saved his business, adding that he would remain eternally grateful for the former President’s intervention. He described the former President as a man of uncommon integrity, humility and simplicity, who devoted much of his life to the service of Nigeria. “To the nation, he was a President and a statesman. To me and my family, he was much more. He was a father figure, a cherished family friend and a source of wisdom, encouragement and comfort,” he said. The BUA chairman, who said he was unable to attend the event because of a previously scheduled engagement in London, expressed regret over his absence. He also announced a pledge of N500 million towards the purchase of 1,000 copies of the biography in honour of Buhari. Rabiu said he had authorised Shuaibu to announce the donation on his behalf, describing the book as an important work that would help preserve the former President’s life, service and legacy for generations. He prayed for Allah’s forgiveness for Buhari’s shortcomings, reward for his good deeds and a place for him in Jannatul Firdaus, while also expressing condolences to his family and loved ones. item.title: Gunmen behead, burn 60-year-old man in Cross River
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar Gunmen have killed a 60-year-old man, James Edi Diwa, and set his body and motorcycle ablaze in Boki Local Government Area of Cross River State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 5:20pm along the Isobendeghe–Boje Road, where Diwa, a native of Katchuan in Irruan community, was riding his motorcycle when he was ambushed. The attackers allegedly shot him, beheaded him and set his remains and motorcycle on fire. The Cross River State Police Command disclosed this in a statement on Thursday by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Eitokpah Sunday. According to the police, the deceased’s wife, Mrs Schola Abang, reported the incident at the Boki Divisional Police Headquarters on November 13, 2026, at about 6:10am. The statement said police operatives visited the scene following the report and commenced preliminary investigations. “The Cross River State Police Command has commenced an investigation into the gruesome murder of a 60-year-old man, identified as James Edi Diwa, who was allegedly ambushed and killed by unidentified gunmen along the Isobendeghe–Boje Road in Boki Local Government Area,” the statement said. The Commissioner of Police, Mr Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, condemned the killing and directed relevant operational and investigative units to intensify efforts to identify and arrest those responsible. The command said no arrest had been made as of the time the statement was issued. Ordue assured residents that the police would work to bring the perpetrators to justice. He urged members of the public to remain calm, refrain from taking the law into their hands and provide credible information that could assist the investigation. item.title: 2027: ACF warns of emerging political violence, urges restraint
item.description: …Forum urges Tinubu, governors to ensure fairness to opposition By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has raised concerns over emerging signs of political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, urging political leaders, security agencies and Nigerians to embrace restraint and protect democratic values. The forum warned that provocative demonstrations, stone-throwing, abusive chants and attacks on individuals could undermine the country’s democratic process and heighten political tensions. In a statement issued by its National Publicity Secretary, Prof. Tukur Muhammad-Baba, the ACF described the development, particularly in major urban centres, as unacceptable, dangerous and condemnable. It expressed concern over reports and videos circulating in conventional and social media showing acts of provocation directed at politically exposed personalities and other high-profile individuals. The forum also condemned the use of physical violence, looting and arson to express political grievances, warning that abusive reactions to such incidents could further escalate tensions. According to the ACF, although political violence is not new in Nigeria’s electoral history, the country should have moved beyond practices that undermine its democratic development and contradict its societal values. It warned that political intolerance, incivility and disregard for law and order posed serious threats to democratic progress and the country’s future. The forum urged Nigerians to embrace calmness and civility, stressing that the legitimate way to express political dissatisfaction was through the use of their Permanent Voter Cards to vote in accordance with the law. It called on community stakeholders, socio-cultural organisations, trade groups, non-governmental organisations, traditional rulers, religious leaders and other citizens to intensify public enlightenment on the dangers of political intolerance and electoral violence. The ACF also urged political office holders, particularly President Bola Tinubu and state governors, to demonstrate fairness, equity and tolerance towards perceived or actual political opponents. It further called on authorities to ensure that opposition parties had unhindered access to public facilities for their campaign activities. The forum urged security agencies to respond firmly but professionally to emerging threats through coordinated and intelligence-driven measures. While commending the recent presidential pardon granted to citizens arrested in connection with the violence, the ACF said attention should now shift towards preventive measures to avert further incidents. It stressed that protecting democratic values and ensuring peaceful political activities ahead of the 2027 elections required collective responsibility from political leaders, security agencies and citizens. item.title: I never planned to have two wives, 18 children – Veteran actor Oga Bello
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Adebayo Salami, popularly known as Oga Bello, has revealed that he never envisaged having two wives and 18 children, saying he initially wanted a simple family life with just one wife. The 73-year-old actor made the revelation during an appearance on the Talk to B podcast, where he spoke about his marriage, family and how life took a different turn from what he had originally planned. Salami said his initial dream was to have a small family, inspired by the marriage of his godfather, Femi Okunnu, whose lifestyle he admired. “I never planned to have a large family. All I wanted was a simple life with my wife, but life took a different direction. “Today, I see my children as part of my destiny,” he said. He recalled how he and his wife enjoyed spending time together, particularly having breakfast before he left for work, describing the arrangement as the kind of family life he had always wanted. However, he said his growing fame changed the course of his personal life and made it difficult to maintain the arrangement he had initially envisioned. The actor also recounted an incident in which two women gave birth to his children within the same week, describing the experience as overwhelming. According to him, he was making preparations for the naming ceremony of one child when he received news that another woman had also delivered a baby for him. Despite the unexpected expansion of his family, Salami said he had no regrets, noting that he now considers his large family part of his destiny. The veteran actor has two wives and 18 children, comprising nine sons and nine daughters. One of his children is popular Nollywood actor and filmmaker Femi Adebayo, and another named Tope Adebayo, who is also an actor. He also disclosed that he never imagined some of his children would eventually follow his footsteps into the entertainment industry. item.title: VeryDarkMan hospitalised in China after severe malaria scare
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Social media activist Martins Otse, popularly known as VeryDarkMan, says he nearly died after developing what doctors in China described as a life-threatening form of malaria. In a video shared on Thursday, the 32-year-old said he was admitted to hospital and placed in quarantine after his condition worsened. He said he had initially ignored a doctor’s warning and taken oral medication obtained through members of the Nigerian community in China. VeryDarkMan said he first visited a hospital where tests showed he had malaria. According to him, a doctor warned that it was a severe case requiring urgent treatment through his veins. He said he later contacted a doctor friend in Nigeria, who reportedly told him it was a common form of malaria. Doubting the Chinese doctor’s advice, VeryDarkMan said he left the hospital and sought medication. “Before I left, the doctor looked at me and told me, ‘They have to make things go through your veins. Oral is not going to work. It’s going to make it worse,’” he said. VeryDarkMan said the first medication he received had expired, so he asked for another dose. He initially felt better after taking it, but said his condition deteriorated that night. “My brothers and sisters, yesterday night, I swear to God, I nearly died, bro. No jokes. Exactly what the doctor said. The drugs turned against me. It became two times worse,” he said. He said he returned to hospital and was told to remain there. Doctors initially proposed seven days in quarantine but reduced the period to four days after assessing his condition, according to the activist. VeryDarkMan urged Nigerians to seek proper medical attention and called for greater awareness of severe malaria. He also appealed to the Federal Government to strengthen malaria prevention and mosquito-control efforts. Nigeria has one of the world’s highest malaria burdens. Severe malaria can cause life-threatening complications and requires urgent medical care. The post VeryDarkMan hospitalised in China after severe malaria scare appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Launches Worldwide To Near-Perfect Reviews
item.description: Gamers around the world got their first taste of “Grand Theft Auto VI” on Wednesday, as critics heaped praise on one of the most anticipated video game releases ever. The latest installment of the crime franchise comes 13 years after the last full edition broke sales records and became one of the most profitable entertainment products of all time. The series lets players live out gangster fantasies, smash up cars and fight whoever they choose in a fictionalized US city populated by lowlifes, sex workers and thugs. “GTA VI” launched first in New Zealand at midnight local time (1100 GMT Wednesday) and is rolling out around the world as each market reaches midnight. New Zealander Luke Starik was among the first to play, and his character did not last long. “Wasted already. First one, didn’t survive long,” he told AFP, laughing. “This is one of the big things in my life…I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time,” Riley Fennel, an Australian student visiting Tokyo, told AFP. Review aggregator Metacritic gave the game a score of 99 out of 100. A 42-year-old gamer wrote on a German-language Reddit forum that he had taken time off work to play all night. By 1:20 am, he was already in bed with a headache, still blown away by the game. “Thirteen years ago, with a game like this, I’d have played until six in the morning,” the gamer wrote. In the game’s official Reddit forum, people raved about improved interactive elements, such as being able to push a stranded ski jet back in the water. “This is amazing!” one person wrote. Analytics firm Omdia estimates “GTA VI” could generate $3.2 billion in sales by the end of the year for studio Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive. PlayStation briefly reported connection issues on its status page before services were restored. People play Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) at Bamboo Gaming Center & Bar in Bangkok on November 19, 2026, on the day of the highly anticipated video game’s release. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ In a review for The Verge titled “GTA VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype,” Andrew Webster wrote that “the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it.” Social media users praised the graphics. “There’s one moment, no spoilers, where the light hits behind one of the characters just right, and I swore I was looking at a real human,” wrote Reddit user No_Strike9652. Before the release, Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business, told AFP the game was an “outlier” in the entertainment industry. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” he said. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said Omdia analyst James McWhirter. Many fans have taken time off to explore the fictional state of Leonida, which is modeled on Florida. “I’m going to take four days off,” said Dmytro
